{"sample_id": "blind-5231c63970d245b1ae4f79d1dc51b504", "theorem": "Let \( x \) and \( y \) be positive integers. If for each positive integer \( n \) we have that

\[
(n y)^{2}+1 \mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1
\]

prove that \( x=1 \).", "assumptions": [], "domain": "bmo", "explicit_subgoals": [], "candidate_text": "Fix positive integers \(x,y\) satisfying the hypothesis for every positive integer \(n\). Suppose, for contradiction, that \(x>1\). Taking \(n=2\), since \(\varphi(2)=1\), gives
\[
4y^2+1\mid x-1.
\]
Choose a prime \(p\mid 4y^2+1\). Then \(p\) is odd, \(p\nmid y\), and \((2y)^2\equiv-1\pmod p\). Hence \(2y\) has order \(4\) modulo \(p\), so \(p\equiv1\pmod4\). In particular, \(p\mid x-1\). Set
\[
s=v_p(x-1),\qquad K=s+1.
\]

Let \(f(T)=y^2T^2+1\). We have \(f(2)\equiv0\pmod p\), while
\[
f'(2)=4y^2\not\equiv0\pmod p.
\]
By Hensel's lemma, there is a unit \(r\pmod{p^K}\), with \(r\equiv2\pmod p\), such that
\[
y^2r^2+1\equiv0\pmod{p^K}.
\]

We now construct an integer \(a\), with \(1<a<2p\), which is a primitive root modulo every power of \(p\). Choose a primitive root \(g\) modulo \(p\), represented by \(1<g<p\). If \(g^{p-1}\not\equiv1\pmod{p^2}\), take \(a=g\). Otherwise take \(a=g+p\); indeed,
\[
(g+p)^{p-1}\equiv g^{p-1}+(p-1)g^{p-2}p\not\equiv1\pmod{p^2}.
\]
Thus \(a\) is primitive modulo \(p\) and
\[
v_p(a^{p-1}-1)=1.
\]
For every positive integer \(m\), LTE gives
\[
v_p\bigl(a^{(p-1)m}-1\bigr)=1+v_p(m),
\]
which shows that \(a\) is a primitive root modulo every \(p^j\).

Furthermore, \(p\nmid\varphi(a)\). Indeed, \(p\nmid a\). If \(p\mid\varphi(a)\), the prime-factor formula for \(\varphi\) would give a prime \(q\mid a\) with \(q\equiv1\pmod p\). Since \(q\le a<2p\), we have \(q\ge p+1\), and \(q\mid a<2q\) forces \(a=q\). This would give \(a\equiv1\pmod p\), contradicting that \(a\equiv g\pmod p\) is a primitive root.

Because \(a\) is a primitive root modulo \(p^K\), choose \(e\ge1\) such that
\[
a^e\equiv r\pmod{p^K},
\]
and put \(n=a^e\). Then
\[
p^K\\mid n^2y^2+1.
\]
Also,
\[
\varphi(n)=\varphi(a^e)=a^{e-1}\varphi(a),
\]
so \(p\nmid\varphi(n)\).

Applying the hypothesis to this \(n\) gives
\[
p^K\mid x^{\varphi(n)}-1.
\]
But since \(p\) is odd, \(p\mid x-1\), and \(p\nmid\varphi(n)\), LTE yields
\[
v_p\bigl(x^{\varphi(n)}-1\bigr)
=v_p(x-1)+v_p(\varphi(n))=s<K,
\]
a contradiction. Therefore \(x>1\) is impossible. Since \(x\) is a positive integer, \(x=1\)."}
